public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 801

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/801](https://www.erdosproblems.com/801)
- [Er79g] Erdős, Paul, *Some old and new problems in various branches of combinatorics*.
  Proceedings of the Tenth Southeastern Conference on Combinatorics, Graph Theory and Computing
  (Florida Atlantic Univ., Boca Raton, Fla., 1979) (1979), 19-37.
- [Al96b] Alon, Noga, *Independence numbers of locally sparse graphs and a Ramsey type problem*.
  Random Structures Algorithms (1996), 271-278.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos801

/--
If $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices containing no independent set on $>n^{1/2}$ vertices then there
is a set of $\leq n^{1/2}$ vertices containing $\gg n^{1/2}\log n$ edges.

Proved by Alon [Al96b].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos801.lean#L1841"]
theorem erdos_801 : answer(True) ↔ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ √n →
      ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), (S.card : ℝ) ≤ √n ∧
        c * √n * Real.log n ≤ (G.induce (S : Set (Fin n))).edgeSet.ncard := by
  sorry

end Erdos801

reformulations.difference: The primary papers use α(G) < ⌊√n⌋ and a set of exactly ⌊√n⌋ vertices. Lean allows α(G) ≤ √n and a set of at most √n vertices. It also uses the natural logarithm, whereas Alon uses base-two logarithms.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: These versions are equivalent with adjusted absolute constants and sufficiently-large thresholds. Lean implies the strict version immediately, padding the selected set to ⌊√n⌋ vertices if necessary. Conversely, replace each vertex of G by two adjacent twins, with complete connections between pairs corresponding to original edges. The resulting graph H has 2n vertices and α(H)=α(G)<⌊√(2n)⌋ for large n. Apply the strict version to H. Its selected set has O(√n) vertices and Ω(√n log n) edges. Only O(√n) edges lie within twin pairs; after discarding these and projecting to G, edge multiplicities are at most four. If necessary, averaging over ⌊√n⌋-element subsets retains a fixed positive fraction of the projected edges. This gives Lean's conclusion. Changing logarithm base only rescales the positive constant. Alon §3 explicitly assumes sufficiently large n.

sources_consulted: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-18.pdf — Erdős, Some old and new problems in various branches of combinatorics, §7(III).
https://web.math.princeton.edu/~nalon/PDFS/indrams1.pdf — Alon, Independence numbers of locally sparse graphs and a Ramsey type problem, Theorem 1.2 and §3.
review.notes: No mathematical defects found. The solved category and positive answer agree with Alon's theorem. The cited external proof compiled successfully; its theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Its natural-square-root and integer-logarithm formulation implies the repository's real-valued asymptotic formulation by adjusting constants. Scratch checks verified the independence-number characterization, uniform eventual quantifiers, finite induced-edge counting, nonvacuity of the graph hypothesis, and boundary cases n=0,1,2; small graph invariants were also evaluated. The live erdosproblems.com page was Cloudflare-blocked despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so the mathematical comparison relied directly on both cited primary papers. The reviewed file and repository worktree were left unchanged.
